name: Taj Mahal
description: An ivory-white marble mausoleum commissioned by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
significance: Finest example of Mughal architecture; inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

name: Qutb Minar
description: A soaring 73-metre minaret of red sandstone built by Qutb ud-Din Aibak. Tallest brick minaret in the world.
significance: Earliest surviving example of Indo-Islamic architecture; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993.

name: Red Fort
description: A massive red sandstone fort built by Emperor Shah Jahan as the residence of Mughal emperors. Now a symbol of India's independence.
significance: Principal residence of Mughal emperors for 200 years; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007.

name: Humayun's Tomb
description: The tomb of Mughal Emperor Humayun built by his widow Bega Begum. First garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent.
significance: Architectural precursor to the Taj Mahal; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993.

name: Ajanta Caves
description: Thirty rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments dating from the 2nd century BCE containing masterpiece paintings and sculptures.
significance: Outstanding examples of Buddhist religious art; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.

name: Ellora Caves
description: A complex of 34 monasteries and temples of Buddhist
year_established: Hindu and Jain faiths excavated over five centuries from solid rock.
image_url: Unique coexistence of three great religions carved from rock; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.

name: Konark Sun Temple
description: A 13th-century sun temple dedicated to the Hindu sun god Surya
year_established: designed as a colossal chariot with 24 stone wheels.
image_url: One of the greatest surviving examples of Orissan temple architecture; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984.

name: Mahabodhi Temple
description: One of the four holy sites related to the life of Buddha. The present temple dates from the 5th-6th centuries CE.
significance: Site where Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2002.

name: Group of Monuments at Hampi
description: Last capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. An extraordinary profusion of temples and palace ruins across a dramatic boulder landscape.
significance: Best preserved ruins of the last great Hindu Kingdom in India; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986.

name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
description: Temples built during the Chandela dynasty renowned for their nagara-style architecture and intricate sculptures.
significance: Unique artistic achievement representing the perfect harmony of medieval Indian architecture and sculpture; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986.

name: Fatehpur Sikri
description: Built by Emperor Akbar as the Mughal capital. Abandoned after only 14 years due to water scarcity. Blends Indian and Persian architectural styles.
significance: Outstanding example of Mughal architecture at its zenith; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986.

name: Sanchi Stupa
description: The Great Stupa at Sanchi is the oldest stone structure in India
year_established: originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.
image_url: Best preserved group of Buddhist monuments in India; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1989.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
description: A Victorian Gothic revival railway station built during the British colonial era. Headquarters of Central Railways and still a functioning station.
significance: Outstanding example of Victorian Gothic Revival blended with Indian architecture; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2004.

name: Jantar Mantar
description: An astronomical observation site comprising 19 major geometric devices for measuring time
image_url: Largest and best preserved of India's historic observatories; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2010.
